The Ekiti State Police Command has arrested 11 suspects over the attack on African Action Congress presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, and other persons at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, the state capital. The police said operatives of the Rapid Response Squad arrested the suspects at their hideouts in the Atikankan area of the town at about 10pm on Friday, following a tip-off. The command disclosed this in a statement issued on Saturday by its Public Relations Officer, Abutu Sunday. The statement read, “The Ekiti State Police Command has arrested eleven (11) suspects in connection with the alleged attack on Mr Omoyele Sowore, an African Action Congress (AAC) presidential aspirant, and other persons at Tawakalitu Restaurant, Dalimore Area of Ado-Ekiti.” It added, “Operatives of the Rapid Response Squad (RRS), based on a credible tip-off, swooped on the hideouts of the suspects at Atikankan Area of Ado-Ekiti at about 10:00 p.m. on Friday, October 30, 2026, where they were arrested.” The suspects were identified as 32-year-old Joseph Tayo, 41-year-old Olatunji Abayomi, 22-year-old Isaac Amba, 18-year-old Kehinde Ajigbana, 18-year-old Tosin David, 18-year-old Solomon Iyanu, 21-year-old Ogunsola Ayomide, 22-year-old Ojo Ayodeji, 32-year-old Kayode Dada, 28-year-old Segun Olatunji and 53-year-old Salami Emmanuel. Items recovered from them included two walkie-talkies, substances suspected to be Indian hemp and Colorado, two Indian hemp crushers, a pack of Rizla, seven ATM cards and 13 mobile phones. Other items were two vehicle keys, a flash drive, a 5G MTN Wi-Fi device, identity cards, eight international passports, three complimentary cards, two suspected criminal charms, a gas lighter and N250. The Commissioner of Police, Falade Michael, assured residents that everyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The statement quoted him as saying that the command “will leave no stone unturned in ensuring that all those found culpable are brought to justice.” Sowore demands sanctions as Ikogosi Marathon bars him from 2026 edition Morning recap: Heatwave bites hard, Sowore Ekiti attack, FG’s transport allowance debate, other top stories Sowore, police trade words over Ekiti attack It added that the command remained committed to protecting lives and property and maintaining peace and security across the state, irrespective of political affiliations. The police also confirmed that Sowore and other victims had recovered from their injuries and been discharged from the hospital. “Meanwhile, the command wishes to reconfirm that all the victims, including Mr Sowore, have received medical attention, been treated and discharged from the hospital,” the statement read. The incident sparked a disagreement between Sowore and the Ekiti State Police Command over the circumstances surrounding the attack, with both sides giving different accounts of what happened at the restaurant. The police had initially described the incident as an altercation involving Sowore and some individuals at Tawakalitu Restaurant, saying the AAC presidential aspirant was injured and taken to hospital for treatment. However, Sowore rejected the police account , insisting that there was no altercation but a coordinated attack by armed men. In a statement, he accused the police of attempting to downplay the incident, saying the Commissioner of Police had visited the scene and seen the injuries sustained by the victims but still described the incident as an altercation. “There was no altercation! We were attacked!” Sowore declared. He later alleged that armed men beat him and threatened to kill him during the incident. He also accused the attackers of targeting him and members of his entourage, raising concerns about their safety. The African Action Congress also raised the alarm over the incident , alleging that Sowore and other party members were attacked in Ado-Ekiti and calling for an investigation into the circumstances of the assault. The disagreement subsequently escalated into a public exchange between the activist and the police , with Sowore challenging the command’s description of the incident and demanding accountability for those responsible. The latest arrests come as the police continue their investigation into the incident.
